Hi @lebaphi - I'm just testing new phase presentation.

It looks good. But, I have a minor vertical alignment issue with this wargame:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/180005315-6970fee8-6cbf-4705-bec9-ba7e0172938d.png)

Oh dear @ShendMikullovci - I think I've just come up with a scary issue.

`START NEW PHASE` is below 3 buttons and above 2 tab buttons.  A bad mouse click for any of them could accidentally trigger a step to a new phase - throwing away routes currently being planned.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/180005889-3183f0c1-dab8-4081-be51-21409687b726.png)

Note: if we do put "next phase" button inside "turn marker" box, we'll need a different shade.  @ShendMikullovci has already suggested shade to use:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/180009100-92f191cf-3d61-4eed-bc6e-c41987ba7d3a.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/180032103-127c4ffd-7c91-4035-a0c2-dd509c5bbeb9.png)

So, @lebaphi - I think the only remaining issue is the "Welcome page" icon alignment: https://github.com/serge-web/serge/pull/1674#issuecomment-1190347468

Thanks guys! 

Love the dimming of the inactive phase. The button inside the box works as well, helps us avoid that accident hopefully. 

Couple of things I wanted to address: 

1. Could we have rounder corners for the action buttons please? It smoothes out the entire look and makes them look more like actual buttons. 
2. I also noticed the button reacts by changing colors upon hover. I don't think that's necessary. A simple dropshadow could do the trick as well:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/180098662-5cdb98ef-d224-4273-bbb6-2d04db25007c.mp4

3. The turn box could do with some rounder corners as well and the same color as the "Game Admin" chat tab. Now that I think of it, why did we settle on the turn box not covering the width of the chat? @lebaphi could be right by putting an outline between the chat and the screen and we might have rushed our hand telling him to remove it...

Essentially, the right hand side has had two main issues regarding visibility: It blends in with the screen (unless we use bright colors) and it blends with itself (chat blends in with upper features/buttons). This latter issue is even more important because the chat and the features that happen to be above it are actually completely unrelated. By placing an outline, we make that dichotomy: 

![New Screen](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/180100546-8a5bc895-2d76-4ce5-ae90-1d5fc1181ca7.png)

Here, the time box (+ features) and the chat are visibly separate from the channels (which maintains our conscious intent on separating them). But more importantly, the time box (+ features) and the chat are _visibly separate from each other_. Our current display doesn't really emphasize that. In this design, every element takes up its adequate spot and is equally visible (I feel like?). The reason why I left the 3 buttons outside of the box (namely, Feedback, Player Log and Intro) is because we want to avoid the user accidentally clicking Start New Phase. This visual separation reduces that risk. What do you guys think?

> Rounder corners

Yes please @lebaphi - let's have rounder corners for the whole "turn progression" box, and the "Start new phase" button.

> I also noticed the button reacts by changing colors upon hover. I don't think that's necessary. A simple dropshadow could do the trick as well:

I've just done some investigating.  I didn't think we had hover action on any other buttons, but it seems most of the `Submit` buttons do change color on hover (I think it's a standard shading that comes with our Material UI toolkit).  The hover shadow is probably too subtle for many Serge users.  So, I think it's right to stick with the hover - we've just got to find the right color.

@ShendMikullovci - there is a gap between the bottom of `Game Admin` and the `New admin message` box.  I don't think this is right, since the `new admin message` box is a part of `Game Admin` - and it's not present for the `Insights` tab.

> @ShendMikullovci - there is a gap between the bottom of `Game Admin` and the `New admin message` box. I don't think this is right, since the `new admin message` box is a part of `Game Admin` - and it's not present for the `Insights` tab.

Hi Ian! You're right. That's because the tabs lack the curvature to make them visually connected to the chat. My bad, lost focus on that. Here we go: 

![Rounded + Connected tabs](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/180598307-ce82adcc-3f10-4ee9-96fb-5bca6fb02089.png)

This got me thinking about the design for the player end. They don't have access to an insights tab, so how would the chat look for them? 

Couple of ideas: 

![Chat Looks for Players](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/180598966-729cb94a-33dc-4e60-aa88-fb76f88ce533.png)

Tab look: The tab is expanded to fit accross the chat window, with the side curvature included. One problem with this is that you can argue that essentially, it's not a tab, since there's no other tabs next to it. Instead, it's more of a header. 

Header 1: Same size without curvature on the bottom placed in the same spot on the X/Y axis. 

Header 2: Larger size (to touch the top of the chat) placed in the same spot on the X/Y axis. For Header 1 and 2 you can argue that the color is inappropriate, since for GC we use the navy blue to indicate the opened tab (which has been clicked on). Players' side doesn't present the option to click (since there's no Insights or other tab to click on).

Header 3: Same as Header 2, except white. Problem here is that it would be laying on top of a white background. Tried a grey one and it's just plain ugly.

We could also go with a no-tab look: 

![No Tab Chat](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/180599826-ed0499b7-fa42-4899-9b78-d08b257fd98a.png)

1st one only has a long underline, similar to the title of a wargame in the admin pages. The 2nd one only underlines the title of the chat. 

Let me know what you guys think!

Hello @ShendMikullovci - thanks for considering this.

Right now, the single-tab issue isn't a great worry.  There _may_ be games where the player is only a member of one channel - so there will only be one tab on the left-hand side.  That's not an issue.

My issue with your designs above remains.  The "new message" box has to be a _child_ of the `Game Admin` component. That's because it isn't present when viewing `Game Insights`.  So, there should not be a space between the list of messages Game Admin messages and the new message box.  The box will not be present for "Insights".

The current layout suggests the new message box isn't directly related to "Game Admin" messages.

Oh! Something like this you mean?: 

![Chat Message Without Box](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/180749561-9d2d0700-8624-463a-9edf-23d07a43cb8a.png)
Yes - that solves the issue.

issues.title: As a Game Designer I need to specify turn interval in months/years
issues.body:
Serge currently allows game turn lengths to be specified using days, hours, minutes, seconds:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/129016115-c59b0f9b-feb3-4c25-abb3-630395456901.png)


For larger scale wargames, the interval could be in months or years, such as each turn spanning a two-month period (Jan21-Feb21, then Mar21-Apr21, then May21-Jun-12, etc). Given the changing length of both of these items (in terms of days), we need an alternate way of specifying game turn length.

So, I _think_ we need a range of turn length strategies:
* days/hours/minutes
* months
* years

Months and years would just take an integer value, using as appropriate in the turn time incrementing.

I _think_ we need a two-step UI.  First select the turn mode, then enter the value.

Here is what the data structure will look like, I guess:
```
export interface MillisecondTurns {
  millis: number
}

export interface MonthTurns {
  months: bigInt
}

export interface YearTurns {
 years: bigInt
}

export type GameTurnLength = MillisecondTurns | MonthTurns | YearTurns

```

Well, to be backward compatible with our current data, it would be:
```
export type GameTurnLength = number | MillisecondTurns | MonthTurns | YearTurns
```

comments.body:
Hello @ShendMikullovci 
this is a feature that overlaps with your other design task (#954)

So far, the turn-period has been expressed in days, hours, or minutes.  All of these can be represented by a single number (milliseconds) in the software, or via a `DD HH:MM:SS` masked text control.

But, in this game they want the turn to move forward 2 months. So, they expect it to step from 1st January to 1st March - **not by 60 days**.  The time period represented by two months changes - so we need a different way of representing that.  While we add `months`, we should probably also support `years`

So that's 3 different ways of expressing the turn size:
* Days/Hours/Minutes
* Months
* Years

I _guess_ we could support this through a drop-down to select the type, then a suitable text field to provide the detail.  Or, a control with three tabs - one for each style. Each tab would contain a suitable edit control - and we'd store the value of the selected tab.

If we need to account for Months and/or Years, we click on “Months” or “Years” mode to do so.

issues.title: Large numbers of forces
issues.body:
For the next wargame, the Game Designer wants lots of people driving ships.

Since we have one "driver" per force, that means we have lots of forces.  So, lots of Blue Forces with one player each, and lots of Red Forces with one player each.

This could introduce problems in these areas:
* In the mapping window Umpire forces can choose which force to view the map as.  This will become a really tall list once we have 20 forces. So, if there are a large number of forces it should turn into a drop-down list
* In the "Perception" dialog the Game Controller specifies which forces can see an asset.  Once we have more than, say, 6 forces we should switch to a drop-down list of toggles, one per force.
* In the Message Channel for `custom` messages we show an icon for each member force at the top. This may need to scroll/wrap once there are a lot of them
* Since all blue forces will have a similar shade, it may become difficult to spot which are a players own asset(s).  So, we could do with introducing some other styling for "own" assets on the map.
* We currently use color to to indicate which force a message comes from.  But. if there are lots of blue forces we will need the force name in the message somewhere.

We probably need to create a wargame with, say, 10 blue forces and 5 red forces, and see where the bottlenecks/problems arise.

Could you do some fresh inspection on where the issues are, and how we can potentially overcome them?

One thought. Here is the game admin column:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/179256579-146a7884-e4f7-440b-8e36-8c9a027446d4.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/179256973-c8574f08-3f81-4cdd-a40e-c395cddf58e8.png)
Hi Ian! How many Forces are we talking about approximatively? Are all of these Forces going to have their own logo/icon?

8 forces for the test, maybe 20 for the real game.

Probably not an icon per force. May have to rely on abbreviated name (letters).

We could also show messages something like the Messenger app:

![Chat Messages Alternative](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/179372191-86e49d45-3202-4215-bc65-43cbd81859aa.png)

Here, on the left, we have our current message layout. As you can see, the only association between the force and their color is made on the left of the message chip where we use color to indicate the force sending the message. We also include the force and role inside the message chip, eating up some space in there. 

Messenger uses a design similar to the right hand side. The picture (or in our case, logo/icon) on the left, next to the message chip. The curvature of the chips adapts to the quantity of the messages to emphasize the message comes from the same person, and avoid repeating the picture (logo/icon) multiple times. Here, force and role are _outside_ of the message chip, leaving all the space to the content being sent. 

The benefits this could have for us are a start to decoupling from this connection we've made between force - color. We could add the force label inside the logo/icon or color sphere. The role would always be shown above the message that's been sent out.
In a game like WATU, where a large number of forces will be operating, without all of them having logos/icons, this might be a good alternative. And it's pretty standard!

Thanks for that fresh thought.

One observation - we need the "time sent" in the message.  Our current implementation may not be enough. Some wargames span multiple days - so we'd need to display date _and_ time for each message. Hmm, this should probably be a setting in the "Overview" panel - since the Game Designer will know if the game is to span whole days or not.

The pattern of curves for multiple messages is an interesting one.  It's a real advantage when one role sends multiple messages - less when conversation flow bounces between 2 or more players.

It "happens" that "RED 2" neatly spans two rows in your example, but once the force is named "BLUE 2" it may not work as well - unless we consciously trim the force name.

It does _feel_ that putting force, role and date-time in 3 corners of the shape spreads them around (to reduce change for word-wrap or overlap), and puts them in predictable locations.

![Chat New](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/179613475-b1fb1f6f-0210-4e28-9f40-56844c51db6d.png)

Added the time stamp inside the message and Force + Role above it. A logo to the side of the message to maintain awareness.
It looks and feels much more like a chat window here. Also, the messages would be separated depending on when they've been sent (date wise).

>The pattern of curves for multiple messages is an interesting one. It's a real advantage when one role sends multiple messages -

Yes, the idea behind it is to make multiple messages from the same person more compact to keep context as well as use up less space. Whenever the conversation flow bounces between 2 or more people having sent singular messages, the message chips don't curve.

>Hmm, this should probably be a setting in the "Overview" panel - since the Game Designer will know if the game is to span whole days or not.

What exactly? Specifying game duration?

> > Hmm, this should probably be a setting in the "Overview" panel - since the Game Designer will know if the game is to span whole days or not.
> What exactly? Specifying game duration?

I was referring to whether date was shown against each message. But, your "new day" marker does the job perfectly well.  I know it feels excessive, but I think we do need the year in there.  The last wargame did span 2021/2022.

> I know it feels excessive, but I think we do need the year in there. The last wargame did span 2021/2022.

Haha! That's the reason I didn't add it in the first place. Here we go: 

![Chat New](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/179860629-acdea9b0-72cb-42c8-a826-cdc4f6abdcc1.png)

Thanks Shend.  Would you propose that we extend this strategy to "Chat channels" in the left-hand side of the UI? I think it could work.
But, originally I think there was some conscious intention to style the "Game Admin" channel differently, as a visual reminder that it's "out of game" messages on the right, and "in game" messages on the left.

> Thanks Shend. Would you propose that we extend this strategy to "Chat channels" in the left-hand side of the UI? I think it could work. But, originally I think there was some conscious intention to style the "Game Admin" channel differently, as a visual reminder that it's "out of game" messages on the right, and "in game" messages on the left.

I think if it's absolutely necessary, then yes. We could format the date/time differently (use numbers only). Though I do agree with you that it goes against our conscious intention to style them differently. We can also try and see how it feels to look at them.

One query on the layout @ShendMikullovci 

Shouldn't there be a _right-angle_ corner on the right of the adjacent messages, too?

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/180178629-73c14f96-cb8a-4118-80eb-d0e9ac98a5bc.png)

> One query on the layout @ShendMikullovci
> 
> Shouldn't there be a _right-angle_ corner on the right of the adjacent messages, too?
> 
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/180178629-73c14f96-cb8a-4118-80eb-d0e9ac98a5bc.png)

The reason Messenger went with only the left side curving is because that's the "identity" side, meaning that's the side that pertains to the interlocuter or the person we're talking to. That way, we perceive not only that the messages are tied together (part of a larger context) but also that they are tied to 1 person (so we wouldn't have to repeat the icon with every message, we'd either keep it by the 1st message or drop it down to the last one).

So, I think we should stick to only the left side having angle curvature.
Sure, ok.

issues.title: General Chat Redesign
issues.body:
I thought of redesigning the general chat, since we've encountered multiple issues in implementing new features (main menu button #1609), bugs (#1619), or improving UI for current features (#1580). 

Came up with this: 

![New General Chat Opened](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/175574524-d94d332b-eae4-417f-ad77-7fbb509207d3.png)

The title of the wargame at the top on the right hand side, accompanied by user's role and force. On the left of the label, the force icon. 
Objectives would appear by clicking on the Force icon, similarly to our current layout. The difference here would be:

1. Bottom of the screen is reserved for messaging (both on the left hand side for channels, and for the right hand side for chatting), as we are used to in most messaging apps.
2. It reinforces the Z pattern that our layouts try to encourage: 

![Z Pattern Example](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/175577400-3b2a3a8b-dcdb-41bf-9664-6ee4e0044869.png)

Here, the user would naturally encounter information following the usual Left-Right, Top-Bottom route.

Home button, would be added next to the Insights, Player Log and Intro buttons. 
The Turn and Phase information also gain importance and centrality here, considering they are crucial info for GC. The action button in light blue against a white background for clarity and presence. 

Furthermore, the chat would become collapsible to give GC the ability to reduce information load: In a busy game, it would be harmful for GC to be distracted by messages from the right hand side, especially if they are redundant. 
The tabs remain similar, with the exception of their appearance: they look like Google Chrome tabs. My girlfriend accidentally stumbled upon an open SERGE Screen and asked me what she was looking at. She then let me know that Insights/Game Admin didn't look like tabs at all. I realized she might be right...
The "Mark All Read" button gets replaced by our usual envelope to maintain uniformity and consistency. All of this gives the chat a much more "chat"-y feel. 

When collapsed, it would look like this: 

![Uploading General Chat Collapsed.png…]()

Reducing information load dramatically and giving a clean look. GC would still have a marker on the chat to remind them of accumulating messages on the chat bar at the bottom right.

Expanded, it would look like this: 

![General Chat Expanded](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/175602797-5a2361d4-14f1-40f4-b926-8ab09fcf5573.png)

Here, GC can view older messages without having to scroll upwards. If messaging is important or task-specific, the user can expand the chat to increase focus. Bold text and message chip for new, unseen messages, that remains bold for a specific time.

I think this would improve game flow, all the while solving some issues we've encountered concerning our current UI.
Let me know what you think.

I'm ok with redesign in general.  But, I do think information is easier to spot if it's in a box.  Lots of SERGE stuff is free text, but parts of the right-hand column are facts/status indicators.  So, for the "Turn number" field, I'd quite like a box with "Turn" along the top, and a large number/label beneath it.  This makes it quicker to scan the UI & determine the turn number.  Same for Force/Role, to be honest.  I don't think there have been instances when I've need to double-check which force a player is in, but I have to double-check (or take note of) their role lots of times.  Having it at the bottom-right of the screen means I can spot it really quicly.

One partially unrelated item.  New players may not be familiar with the rotation between "planning" and "adjudication".  _Maybe_ we should stack the terms up, and use highlighting (and/or a flag indicator) to indicate which phase we are in.

Fully support making admin/insights look more like tabs, but not that only Game Control typically has the "insights" tab - so there is no switching involved for other players.

Note: I don't see the design for the collapsed game admin panel.  I _think_ all players should see Game Admin all the time.  When it contains something like "Adjudication is running over, so next phase will start 15 minutes late. Please grab a coffee."  Messages like these shouldn't be hidden.

> 

Love the turntable idea! 
I know we can spot Force/Role quickly when placed below but I'm not sure that's the case for our users. If there's no value in them having that information available quickly, then sure we can place it below. The other issue with placing the Force/Role text labels below is that it goes against virtually every messaging app/chat setup. 

Here's another look: 

![New General Chat](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/85491794/176288559-815abcd9-f858-44ae-9274-3b8f9c76d7eb.png)

Hmm, maybe it fits in with a RPG interface, where status data is placed around the edge of the screen, including top and bottom.

I like the turn number & phase.  The current time and "start new phase" are linked to this information. Are you able to integrate these two extra fields into your design.  Note: only the Game Controller has "Start new phase" - so most people won't have that button visible.

One last thing. The `insights` and `Game admin` tabs are upside down.  The style you've used is for when they're vertically below the page they relate to.

The 4 icons are neatly displayed in the line, but they have quite different purposes.  The home button is certainly a bigger effect than the others.  Hmm, since the Home button means "leave this game" - maybe there is logic in putting it to the right of the wargame title.  Hmm, you may have suggested this earlier, but in the context of "leave this game", maybe an exit icon would be more logical?
